title: Emergency fund bill for recent hurricane damage
summary: Bill 122 passed first reading on September 4 with seven ayes, one excused and one abstention, and it needs a second reading because the Council was not asked to waive that rule. It would allow up to $10 million from the emergency fund for hurricane costs, including up to $1 million for Maui Economic Opportunity. Damage was estimated at $9,929,077, and the County may ask for more funding as departments find more damage.

timeline.text: The hurricane funding bill passed first reading with seven ayes, one excused and one abstention (a member sitting out).
One member said he would abstain because the bill includes money for a past employer.
A cost estimate read aloud put hurricane damage at $9,929,077, including $4 million for debris removal.
The administration asked for quick action so departments can keep responding to community needs and emergency repairs.
Up to $1 million would go to Maui Economic Opportunity for rebuilding and recovery help.
